1. Core Clinical Tension: A 59-year-old previously healthy man presenting with extensive disseminated crusted, ulcerated skin and oral mucosal lesions, an oral exophytic mass, firm inguinal adenopathy, and a pigmented hyperkeratotic plantar lesion, creating an intense diagnostic dilemma between metastatic melanoma with widespread cutaneous metastases versus synchronous endemic mucocutaneous leishmaniasis and malignant melanoma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs in December 2018 upon hospital admission for evaluation of widespread mucocutaneous ulcerations and the plantar pigmented mass, before biopsy of the plantar lesion and external laboratory PCR testing returned.
3. Differential Distinctions: Metastatic melanoma can cause widespread necrotic and nodular cutaneo-mucosal metastases; however, while biopsy of the plantar lesion confirmed concurrent primary acral melanoma, the disseminated orofacial and mucosal ulcers represented an independent infectious disease confirmed by Leishmania PCR and responsive to liposomal amphotericin B.
case_prompt:
A 59-year-old man of mixed ethnicity, currently unemployed and previously healthy, presents to the hospital with a two-month history of widespread, evolving skin and oral lesions. The illness began as an erythematous-crusted lesion over the mental protuberance of the chin that progressively spread over two months to involve the frontal and occipital scalp, nasal septum, ears, hands, and lower extremities. Concurrently, he noted new sores inside his mouth.

On physical examination, the patient has scattered ulcers across the face, lower labial mucosa, and the left oral commissure. Examination of the oral cavity reveals a pseudomembrane over the marginal gingiva and an exophytic nodule on the left labial mucosa. On full-body dermatologic examination, enlarged, firm lymph nodes are palpable in the left inguinal region. In addition, an extensive, irregular melanocytic lesion presenting an area of hyperkeratosis with a grey-bluish center is identified on the plantar aspect of the left foot. Triage evaluations and staging workup are initiated upon admission.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Metastatic Melanoma / Primary Cutaneous Malignancy with distant metastases
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The patient indeed possessed a primary cutaneous malignancy confirmed on biopsy of the plantar foot with regional lymph node involvement, but this did not account for the widespread infectious mucocutaneous ulcerations which resolved with antiparasitic therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient was biopsied and the diagnostic hypothesis of melanoma was confirmed.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: An exophytic nodule in the labial mucosa with adjacent mucosal ulcers and hard lymphadenopathy strongly mimicked head-and-neck carcinoma, but the lesions represented inflammatory granulomatous changes rather than mucosal carcinoma.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Oral cavity clinic-examination showed scattered ulcers on the face, lower labial mucosa, and on the left lip commissure, pseudomembrane on the marginal gingiva, and an exophytic nodule in the left labial mucosa ( Figure 4).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis (coexisting with Cutaneous Melanoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis of disseminated mucocutaneous leishmaniasis was confirmed by a positive Montenegro skin test and outside PCR analysis, leading to successful treatment with liposomal amphotericin B concurrently with surgical management of his independent melanoma.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Patient was Montenegro intradermal test positive and was admitted at the University Hospital in December 2018. The PCR analysis was perfomed in a laboratory outside the hospital.

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint enforced prior to melanoma histopathology and outside PCR results. Highlights synchronous occurrence of acral melanoma and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.
